F-country-China: Five evidence items involve firms located in China. Sunstar Guangzhou recalled GUM toothpaste, packed in China, for a cGMP deviation [E1]. Wuxi Medical Instrument Factory recalled ViaMed Alcohol Prep Pads for lack of sterility assurance and cGMP deviations observed at the manufacturing site [E2]. Qinhuangdao Zizhu Pharmaceutical recalled bulk levonorgestrel, estradiol and estriol for cGMP deviations and lack of quality assurance [E5]. Zhejiang Jingwei Pharmaceutical recalled a povidone iodine antiseptic ointment whose declared inactive ingredients did not match the product [E7]. Huijing (Shanghai) Bio-tech recalled subpotent acne treatment pads [E10]. Three further events were initiated by US firms but concern product manufactured in China: Alkano Chemicals recalled thyroid powder produced by Sichuan Friendly Pharmaceutical [E4], The Mentholatum Co. recalled a capsaicin patch manufactured in Guangdong [E6], and Shane Erickson recalled hand sanitiser made in China [E9].
F-country-Spain: One evidence item is a firm located in Spain: Medichem S.A. of Barcelona recalled chlorhexidine gluconate API batches after detecting the gram-negative bacillus Serratia marcescens, Class I [E1]. Six further events were initiated by US firms but concern product manufactured at Spanish sites. Breckenridge Pharmaceutical recalled duloxetine delayed-release capsules manufactured by Towa Pharmaceutical Europe, S.L. of Martorelles, Barcelona, on four occasions, all for N-nitroso-duloxetine impurity above the FDA recommended interim limit [E4][E5][E6][E9]. Sandoz recalled Introvale and Estarylla contraceptive tablets, manufactured by Laboratorios Leon Farma S.A. in Spain, for tablets out of sequence [E7][E10], and Xiromed recalled Altavera, also manufactured by Laboratorios Leon Farma S.A., for mislabelling of the generic name [E8].
F-country-Switzerland: One evidence item is a firm located in Switzerland: F. Hoffmann-LaRoche Ltd. of Basel recalled Cymevene 500 mg powder for infusion for lack of assurance of sterility arising from container closure issues with the bulk batch, Class II [E2]. One further event was initiated by a US firm but concerns product manufactured at a Swiss site: Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corp. recalled physician sample bottles including Exforge HCT, manufactured by Novartis Pharma Stein AG in Stein, Switzerland, for chemical contamination with Darocur 1173, a photo-curing agent used in inks on shrink-wrap sleeves [E8]. The remaining evidence items involve firms and manufacturing sites outside Switzerland [E1][E3][E4][E5][E6][E7][E9][E10].
F-country-United_Arab_Emirates: Four evidence items are firms located in the United Arab Emirates, all Sun Pharma entities. Sun Pharma Global Inc. of Dubai recalled venlafaxine hydrochloride extended-release tablets that failed dissolution specifications at the 12-month stability time point [E1]. Sun Pharma Global Fze of Sharm recalled levetiracetam extended-release tablets that failed dissolution at the 6-month time point [E3]; ketorolac tromethamine ophthalmic solution that did not meet the specification limit for particles present in solution [E4]; and alendronate sodium tablets where the highest unknown impurity exceeded the specification limit at the 3-month stability time point [E9]. All four are Class II. The remaining evidence items are recalls by firms located in the United States [E2][E5][E6][E7][E8][E10].
